mission: The AI Office is the European Commission's centre for implementing the EU AI Act, especially the rules for general-purpose AI (GPAI) models. It can evaluate GPAI models, demand information and risk-mitigation measures from providers, and fine them; it also coordinates national regulators and promotes trustworthy AI in Europe.

key_work.title: General-Purpose AI Code of Practice
key_work.plain_summary: A voluntary code, written by independent experts, that GPAI providers can sign to show they meet the AI Act. Its Safety and Security chapter covers how makers of the most powerful models assess and reduce systemic risks.

key_work.title: Enforcement framework of the AI Act
key_work.plain_summary: Explains the Office's investigative and sanctioning powers, which apply from 2 August 2026, including fines of up to 3% of global turnover for GPAI providers.

key_work.title: Signatory Taskforce of the GPAI Code of Practice
key_work.plain_summary: A forum chaired by the AI Office where signatories work through how to apply the code — e.g. using post-market monitoring of model usage as part of systemic-risk assessment.

key_work.title: Guidelines for providers of general-purpose AI models
key_work.plain_summary: Commission guidance on which models count as GPAI and as 'GPAI with systemic risk', and what obligations follow.

status_note: set up inside the European Commission in 2024; its enforcement powers over general-purpose AI models started on 2 August 2026, and it sent its first formal requests for information to model providers on 29 August 2026.
status_raw: active — set up inside the European Commission in 2024; its enforcement powers over general-purpose AI models started on 2 August 2026, and it sent its first formal requests for information to model providers on 29 August 2026.

size_note: The Commission says the AI Office employs more than 125 staff in 6 units, including an 'AI Safety' unit (A3).

warnings.text: The most advanced GPAI models can pose systemic risks: CBRN incidents, loss of control, cyber offence, harmful manipulation and threats to fundamental rights.
AI agents built on GPAI models raise new transparency and safety issues.
Pre-deployment testing alone is not enough; how models behave in real use must be monitored.

recommendations.text: Providers of systemic-risk GPAI models should assess and mitigate those risks, report serious incidents and ensure cybersecurity.
Use independent external model evaluations and post-market monitoring.
Tell users when they are interacting with AI and label AI-generated content (transparency rules from Aug 2026).
